summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to discuss, plan, and ship all 5 v1.1 hardening phases (51-55: crypto-signature, FUSE durability, supply-chain, E2E typing, large-file refactor) in parallel using git worktrees. Ship Phase 51 first through the full verify/secure/validate/simplify/CodeRabbit/ship/resolve-pr-reviews loop before touching other phases.
summary.outcome: All 5 phases discussed and planned (21 total plans across phases, each in an isolated worktree). Phase 51 executed, verified (caught a cross-crate build break), secured (15/15 threats closed), validated (Nyquist-compliant), simplified, CodeRabbit-reviewed (fixed 5 of 7 zeroization findings), shipped as PR #529 — including diagnosing and fixing a critical S3 zeroization regression that caused 48/89 SDK E2E failures in CI.

repo: GSD executor's commit style (`feat 51-03: …`) is non-conventional and systematically fails the repo's `pr-release-preview` required CI check on any PR touching versioned packages. Requires `git filter-branch --msg-filter` reword before the PR can merge.
`required_signatures: false` on main, so filter-branch rewrites that drop SSH signatures are safe.

Background GSD agents on this Claude Code harness DO have `Tools: *` and CAN nest sub-agents — the manager.md blanket 'no nesting in background on Claude Code' guardrail is stale/wrong for this session.
`winfsp` cannot compile on macOS (build script + `windows_core` errors). Windows-only changes must ride CI for correctness gating.
Per-worktree `pnpm i` is the correct approach for dependencies in isolated git worktrees — symlinking node_modules causes hook/merge failures.
The GSD commit helper reports `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit lands. Always verify with `git log --oneline -1`.
CodeRabbit bundles all nitpicks in the PR review body, not inline threads — `/resolve-pr-reviews` searching for threads finds 0; must parse `pulls/{N}/reviews[].body`.

Phase 51's `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` executor gate never compiles the `cipherbox-desktop` crate, so cross-crate type-change cascades (e.g. `unwrap_key` return type) can break desktop consumers silently.

code.finding: S3 added a `finally { params.ipnsPrivateKey.fill(0) }` block to `createAndPublishIpnsRecord`, but the client caches `folder.ipnsKeypair.privateKey` in `folderTree` and passes that same long-lived buffer to every publish. Zeroing a caller-owned buffer caused every 2nd+ folder operation to derive the public key from zeros → wrong IPNS name → 400 from the API. Fix: remove the `finally` zeroization; `cas.ts` documents 'callers are responsible'.
Reuses the same `params.ipnsPrivateKey` buffer across retries. The caller-owns-key contract is documented here but was violated by the callee's `finally` zeroization added in Phase 51 S3.

S3 changed `unwrap_key` to return `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`, cascading to this desktop consumer which the executor's `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` gate never compiled. Initial hotfix used `.to_vec()` (loses Zeroizing); final fix changed the SDK state field type to `RwLock<Option<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>>` and stores the value directly.

Field `root_folder_key` changed from `RwLock<Option<Vec<u8>>>` to `RwLock<Option<zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>>` as part of CodeRabbit finding #3 fix. `root_ipns_private_key` was left as plain `Vec` (HKDF-derived, deferred).

Folder-key cache changed from `HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>` to `HashMap<String, Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>` (CodeRabbit #6). `spawn_file_meta_reencrypt` worker's `[u8;32]` key arrays wrapped in `Zeroizing` (CodeRabbit #7). `resolve_folder_key_cached` return type kept as `Vec<u8>` to callers but stores zeroizing internally.

S1 value-anchoring strengthened to verify `/ipfs/` prefix in `record.value`. S2 partial-fields fail-closed: rejects records missing `signatureV2`, `data`, or `pubKey` fields instead of silently skipping verification.
S2 partial-fields fail-closed applied (mirrors API change). Simplify: three identical base64-decode-and-map-err blocks deduped into a local closure `decode_field`.

Plan correctly flagged buffer-reuse risk for `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` but missed the identical risk for `createAndPublishIpnsRecord`, which caused the S3 regression. Mock-based unit test for this callee masked the real round-trip behavior.

workflow: Git worktree isolation per phase (`git worktree add <path> <branch>` + `pnpm i`) is the correct pattern for parallel GSD background planning agents to avoid `index.lock` collisions and branch-switch interference.

The `git filter-branch --msg-filter 'sed -E ...'` approach enables non-interactive bulk commit message rewrites without `git rebase -i` (which requires interactive input). Drops signatures but safe when `required_signatures: false`.

Mock-based unit tests for security-critical paths can pass while the real implementation regresses. The S1 spec mocked `parseIpnsRecord`, hiding the fact that the S3 `finally` zeroization would break real cross-package key reuse patterns.
When a background agent is cut off by a session limit, check `git log` and worktree state before restarting — agents often commit their final work before terminating.
For Rust cross-crate type changes, run `cargo check --workspace` (not just `-p <one-crate>`) as a final gate before committing — executor-scoped tests miss downstream consumers.

CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed`) returning 0 findings after fixes is reliable confirmation, but the PR-level review (triggered on push) provides additional findings not in the CLI scope.

When doing a comprehensive security zeroization sweep, audit every public function's ownership contract at the boundary, not just the crates under test — the regression came from a callee overstepping a documented caller-owns-key contract in a different package.

friction: Two session limit interruptions required context reconstruction and agent restart mid-workflow.

GSD executor commit style (`feat 51-03:`) systematically breaks the repo's Release Preview CI check — required discovering this only after the PR was open, then manually rewording 13 commits via filter-branch and force-pushing.
Phase 51 planning agent initially launched without worktree isolation, sharing the main working tree. Had to stop the agent, create a proper worktree, and restart.
Background bash poll for CodeRabbit completion exited immediately after force-push before CI had registered new checks — required manual re-arm.
The default `/gsd:ship` PR title format (`Phase 51: <slug>`) is non-conventional and would fail `lint-pr-title` CI — had to construct a conventional title manually.
Rust `cargo fmt` reformatted entire `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs` (279 lines) when touching two lines — had to revert and apply minimal surgical edits to avoid polluting the PR diff.
CodeRabbit's PR review findings require parsing the review body text (not inline threads), making automated resolution non-obvious.

The S3 zeroization regression (48/89 E2E failures) required extensive local reproduction infrastructure: rebuilding full package chain, restarting API, adding temporary diagnostic interceptors across three files, running multiple cargo check invocations.
